`static_files.read_file(root_dir, requested_path)` (see seed/README.md) hands back the bytes of a file under a content root; today it's a one-line `os.path.join` + `open`, which trusts `requested_path` completely. We're about to let outside callers pass that path straight from user input, so it needs to be bulletproof:

- The resolved file must always stay inside `root_dir`. Reject any `requested_path` that contains a `..` path segment at all — even one that would mathematically cancel out and still resolve inside `root_dir` — and reject a path that starts with a slash or backslash, or a Windows drive letter like `C:\...`. Treat `\` and `/` as equivalent separators throughout.
- Reject a `requested_path` containing a NUL byte or any other control character (a code point below `0x20`) — raise our own error for these rather than letting a low-level exception leak out.
- Raise `static_files.PathSecurityError` (add this exception) for every case above, and also for a `requested_path` that resolves to a directory instead of a file, or to a path that doesn't exist — don't let `IsADirectoryError`/`FileNotFoundError` escape either.
- Cap how deep a legitimate request can go: more than 6 directories of nesting is also a `PathSecurityError`, even when the path never leaves `root_dir`.
- Don't over-correct: filenames are free to contain dots that aren't a `..` segment (`archive..old.txt`), unicode text, spaces, and even literal `%2e%2e`-style percent sequences — none of that is URL-decoded or expanded, so treat it as an ordinary filename and serve it.
